documentTitle: Employee-paid state disability, paid-leave and long-term-care payroll assessments (2026)
note: Employee contribution rates only. Employer shares are out of scope: this calculator models the employee's paycheck. Every rate below is verified against the cited official publication.

programs.label: Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)
programs.reference: Colorado FAMLI 2026: total premium 0.88% of wages split evenly, so the employee pays 0.44% on wages up to the $184,500 federal Social Security wage cap.

programs.label: Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFMLI)
programs.reference: CT Paid Leave: employers deduct a 0.5% worker contribution via payroll deduction.
programs.note: Connecticut caps contributions at the Social Security contribution base, but that cap is not applied here because it could not be confirmed against a machine-readable official 2026 publication. The manifest discloses the omission.

programs.label: Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI)
programs.reference: Hawaii DLIR Disability Compensation Division, 2026 Maximum Weekly Wage Base (December 10, 2025): employee share capped at 0.5% of weekly wages and a $7.50 maximum weekly deduction.

programs.label: Paid Medical Leave (PFML)
programs.reference: Massachusetts DFML 2026: up to 0.28% of eligible wages withheld for medical leave; individual contributions capped by the Social Security taxable maximum.

programs.label: Paid Family Leave (PFML)
programs.reference: Massachusetts DFML 2026: up to 0.18% of eligible wages withheld for family leave; individual contributions capped by the Social Security taxable maximum.

programs.label: Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI)
programs.reference: New Jersey DOL 2026 worker rate: D.I. 0.0019 on the $171,100 worker taxable wage base.

programs.label: Family Leave Insurance (FLI)
programs.reference: New Jersey DOL 2026 worker rate: F.L.I. 0.0023 on the $171,100 worker taxable wage base.

programs.label: Disability Benefits (DBL)
programs.reference: New York Workers' Compensation Law 209(3)(a): one-half of one percent of wages, not in excess of sixty cents per week.

programs.label: Paid Family Leave (PFL)
programs.reference: New York Paid Family Leave 2026: 0.432% of gross wages, capped at $411.91 for the year.

programs.label: Paid Leave Oregon
programs.reference: Paid Leave Oregon 2026: total contribution 1% of gross wages up to $184,500; employees pay 60% of that (0.6%).

programs.label: Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI)
programs.reference: Rhode Island DLT 2026: 1.1% employee wage deduction on a $100,000 taxable wage base.
